subject: Metering timestamps drifting across day boundaries — UTC offset impact
messages:
From: finance@acme-corp.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: cloud-billing@awsmarketplace.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected day-bound usage spikes in Nov invoices

Hi Mateo,

We're seeing a series of 11/13 and 11/14 invoice line items that appear shifted by one day according to our ledger. Attached is a small excerpt from our marketplace export (metering_export_20261114.csv) — you can see a cluster of usage rows stamped around 00:00 UTC that have been billed to 11/13 in our system but 11/14 in the marketplace invoice. This is causing our revenue recognition and VAT reporting to be out of alignment.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is ingesting marketplace meter rows using UTC or local timezone boundaries? Our finance ops runs reporting in America/Los_Angeles and this mismatch is triggering tax/period errors.

Thanks,
Sandra Lopez
Finance Ops — Acme Cloud Solutions
fsandralopez@acme-corp.com

Attachment: metering_export_20261114.csv (csv, 2.1 KB)

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: finance@acme-corp.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, cloud-billing@awsmarketplace.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected day-bound usage spikes in Nov invoices

Sandra — thanks for the heads up and the sample export.

Quick summary of what we'll do:
- Neha will pull the raw ingestion logs and the marketplace batch cut boundaries for 11/13-11/15.
- Jonas will run a comparison between Redwood's ingestion timestamp and the marketplace-provided usage_timestamp fields to find any systematic offset.
- I'll coordinate with AWS billing team (cc'd) for confirmation of their day cut (UTC midnight vs. local) and request any clarification around DST or partner-side aggregation windows.

Can you upload the full CSV export and the affected invoice PDF to the Drive link in our related_links so we have the whole evidence chain? If you can also confirm the timezone used for your accounting exports, that helps (looks like America/Los_Angeles from the sample).

I'll follow up by EOD Wednesday with a short triage summary.

— Mateo Alvarez
Senior Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com

Attachment: none

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: finance@acme-corp.com, cloud-billing@awsmarketplace.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected day-bound usage spikes in Nov invoices — ingestion log findings

Team / Sandra — quick findings from raw logs and the marketplace export:

1) Ingestion timestamps: Redwood's collector stores all marketplace rows with the marketplace-provided usage_timestamp and also records local ingestion_time in UTC. For the batch windows around 2026-11-13/14 the marketplace export shows usage_timestamps between 2026-11-14T00:00:00Z and 2026-11-14T01:15:00Z.

2) Marketplace aggregation: AWS is aggregating some partner-side meter events into the previous UTC day when they apply partner corrections. In this case a correction with event_time 2026-11-14T00:02:00Z was applied to the 11/13 bucket on the AWS-side ledger.

3) Local accounting view: Your accounting system (America/Los_Angeles) considers 2026-11-13T17:00:00-08:00 to 2026-11-14T16:59:59-08:00 as the reporting day for 11/14. That creates a mismatch — the AWS ledger moved a small correction back to the previous UTC date, which then shows as a day-earlier charge in the marketplace invoice while your local reports still attribute it to 11/14.

Attached are two exports: ingest-log-20261114.txt (showing the ingestion_time and usage_timestamp) and a short CSV showing the single correction row with marketplace_bucket=2026-11-13.

Action items:
- Jonas: can you produce a delta report (Redwood timestamp vs AWS bucket) for the affected invoice lines and tag rows that were re-bucketed by AWS corrections?
- Mateo: please ask Acme to confirm whether they want us to re-map marketplace-billed rows into their local accounting day or to provide a reconciliation file they ingest to match Redwood and AWS.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Billing Engineer — Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: ingest-log-20261114.txt (txt, 7.4 KB); correction-row-sample.csv (csv, 0.6 KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: finance@acme-corp.com, cloud-billing@awsmarketplace.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected day-bound usage spikes in Nov invoices — delta report and proposed reconciliation

All — attached is a short delta report (generated from our metering table) that highlights 12 rows where AWS applied a correction that changed the billing bucket from 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-13 (see column aws_bucket_date vs redwood_usage_date). Excerpt: 

"id,usage_timestamp,aws_bucket_date,redwood_usage_date,units"
"12345,2026-11-14T00:02:15Z,2026-11-13,2026-11-14,4"
"12346,2026-11-14T00:47:03Z,2026-11-13,2026-11-14,2"

Root cause summary: AWS applied partner-side corrections that retroactively moved a small set of meter events into the previous UTC day. Redwood stores the original usage_timestamp and attributes by UTC day when creating invoices, but your local accounting (Pacific) maps timestamps to local calendar days for VAT cutoffs. The mismatch therefore appears when AWS reroutes events between UTC day buckets.

Proposed reconciliation options (pick one):
A) Redwood provides a reconciliation mapping file (CSV) for your accounting system that maps marketplace invoice lines to your local reporting date. We can generate this per-invoice for the impacted period.
B) Acme chooses to reconcile to the marketplace invoice (AWS bucket dates) and we provide a small adjustment file for your ledger to apply to the Nov period.
C) If you prefer system-side fixes: we can add a Delta flag on invoices that highlights rows re-bucketed by marketplace corrections; this would help downstream accounting teams ignore those lines or treat them as adjustments.

Next steps: if Acme picks A or B we'll run a formal evidence bundle and deliver the reconciliation CSV plus the ingestion logs (metering_export_20261114.csv, ingest-log-20261114.txt). If A, we can include a column local_reporting_date that maps to America/Los_Angeles.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Revenue Data Platform — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachment: delta-report-20261120.csv (csv, 1.8 KB)
